sub-cytotoxic methyl jasmonate attenuates matrix metalloprotein 14 expression by decreasing specificity protein 1 expression and binding, thus inhibiting migration, invasion and tube formation of gastric cancer cells.
methyl jasmonates attenuate the migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of human gastric cancer cells via down-regulation of Sp1-mediated matrix metalloproteinases 14 expression.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sub-cytotoxic methyl jasmonate attenuates the migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of human gastric cancer cells through decreasing the MMP-14 and its downstream gene VEGF expression via down-regulating the transcription factor Sp1.

sub-cytotoxic (non-lethal) MJ attenuates the migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of SGC-790 and MKN-44 cells by decreasing the expression of MMP-14, which may be mediated by decreasing the expression and binding of Sp1 on the MMP-14 promoter.
sub-cytotoxic concentrations of MJ can inhibit the migration, invasion, and angiogenesis, and that this effect is achieved through down-regulation MMP-14 via the Sp1/MMP-14 signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MJ can be used as a promising agent for gastric cancer prevention.
MJ may serve as a potential agent for gastric cancer therapy.
sub-cytotoxic (i.e. 0.05 to ~0.2 mM, depending on the cancer cells) MJ can be used as a potential chemotherapeutic agent for gastric cancer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sub-cytotoxic (non-toxic) MJ can be a promising agent in cancer therapy.
sub-cytotoxic methyl jasmonate can be a promising anti-metastatic agent for gastric cancer treatment.
sub-cytotoxic concentrations of MJ can inhibit the migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of human gastric cancer cells through the down-regulation of MMP-14.
